nwi-wetlands.geojson.query: where 1=1, geometry = DNR Major 8 'Leech Lake River' (HUC8 07010102) polygon from watershed-whole-basin.geojson, spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects; fetched in 500-feature chunks by OBJECTID
nwi-wetlands.geojson.simplification: Douglas-Peucker ~7 m (same tolerance as the parcels pull)
nwi-wetlands.geojson.route: ArcGIS REST chunked pull (see caveats). The synthesis-preferred per-county FileGDB download is not offered by FWS: downloads are whole-state only (MN FileGDB zip 2.19 GB, GeoPackage zip 4.14 GB, https://documentst.ecosphere.fws.gov/wetlands/data/State-Downloads/MN_geodatabase_wetlands.zip, Last-Modified 2026-10-02), and the mapper's download-by-watershed is 'still under development'. Measured download speed from this VM ~0.56 MB/s, so the state FileGDB would take ~65 minutes; the clipped count (71,539, not the 264,701 bbox count) makes the REST chunked pull feasible, so it was used.
nwi-wetlands.geojson.vintage: Vintage is PER PROJECT, not a single date: the Data_Source 'Image Year' layer clipped to HUC8 gives IMAGE_YR counts {'2014': 1}. The 1979-88 photography cited in inventory 3.5 is what the 2010 lakeshore model used; it is NOT the current NWI vintage for this area. See data_source_counts / source_type_counts for the project sources.
nwi-wetlands.geojson.caveats: USFWS National Wetlands Inventory, Version 2 Surface Waters and Wetlands (Cowardin-classified wetland + deepwater polygons). Intended use scale 1:12,000 per NWI metadata; NWI is not a legal or regulatory delineation of wetland boundaries. VERY HEAVY layer (71,539 polygons) -- needs simplification (done, ~7 m) and zoom-gating like parcels before publishing. Vintage is PER PROJECT, not a single date: the Data_Source 'Image Year' layer clipped to HUC8 gives IMAGE_YR counts {'2014': 1}. The 1979-88 photography cited in inventory 3.5 is what the 2010 lakeshore model used; it is NOT the current NWI vintage for this area. See data_source_counts / source_type_counts for the project sources.
